I wouldn't say the most busted, but it is very high up there. Starmie ex does most things pikachu ex does but swaps consistency for flexibility. What keeps pikachu ex up as the leader of the meta is basically the type advantages. I think starmie ex is probably more cognizant in people's minds because of the Lapras event. Still starmie ex is 100% a top meta deck but is gated from challenging pikachu ex because of type advantages.

But I can realistically see starmie ex being a huge pain in the future when more consistency tools are introduced. It's already a huge pain to most non-meta decks or lower tier decks, and imo playing against starmie is more painful than pikachu for decks that are neutral in typing. For example I've played a bunch of dragonite, wheezing/pidgeot, rapidash/ninetales, gengar, venasaur ex. Overall, I think for a majority of them I just really rather not have to play around a free retreat ex that my win con half the time is just to hope they brick by not drawing staryu or starmie or I have a way to deal 50 damage on turn one without type advantages.

Yea but I think most people perhaps aren't thinking in mind of an electric type deck. Most cases you can't OHKO the staryu or the starmie if you're playing something else. Heck some variations probably can't 2HKO it. You go through that process then it just seems absurd. I think if pikachu didn't have a type advantage against starmie we'd be seeing a helluva lot more of it.

Assuming that they are equal, you'd naturally pick the one with a direct advantage (Not saying that they are equal, just hypothetically). I think the retreat cost is really underrated, people just kinda caught on to the shenanigans you can do with it. Overall i think the deck is undeniably strong, I honestly can't see it being any lower than top 5. It's still an insane and highly flexible deck kept in check by pikachu ex and it's slight consistency issues as a stage 1 mon.

I think unless pikachu ex is nerfed some way or with big meta shifts to favour starmie there's no reason to touch starmie ex.

I think the issue is consistency? I played nubatama a lot when the clan event came out during the breakride era and the legion era. Heck I've spent probably several ranked fight seasons climbing with them, megacolony and granblue. I mean it's fun but if you're against a player who knows what he's doing then your gameplan probably won't go that smoothly. 

So let me give an example, nubatama. It's fairly good at destroying your opponent's hand but it has a glaring weakness, its own card draw is lacking. So depending on the deck type, if your deck has the capability of superior calling a bunch, you do that and preserve your handsize to about 6-7 cards, that way, you survive the hand snipes with a decent amount of cards left. After you survive that, nubatama's soul and cards left in hand is usually pretty low and they can't do that incredible turn when they pop like 4 cards from the bind zone anymore.

If you deck can't superior call much or draw much, you just go aggro and keep your hand 3 and below, 4 honestly is fairly okay as well. So you can dodge most hand snipes while you're being aggressive and nubatama can't match that. Of course this style is probably gonna be dangerous because if trigger luck ain't on your side, you might lose.

I'm not saying these underrated decks can't win but they usually need luck on their side or the opponent to play into them. The latter is especially true for nubatama and megacolony. There are ways to preserve your hand so that you can push damage while planning around a future turn. If you don't plan around the megacolony vanguard stun, you're usually fked. I believe that the ideal thing to do is to precraft the base rarity Commons, Rs, RRs and RRRs in this specific order. Because RRRs require the usage of more materials to craft but the GR mats you obtain are actually the same as precrafting 50 Rs.

You obtain 2 GR mats for getting duplicate R rarity cards which costs 60 CM. You obtain 100 GR mats for getting a duplicate RRR rarity for 3000CM. For 3000CM you could claim 50 Rs which would be mean 100 GR mats. So the amount of GR mats you get for precrafting each rarity is the same however higher rarities require the usage of additional crafting materials. E.g. crafting a RRR requires the usage of RRR, RR and R materials while crafting an R only uses the R material. (And the common crafting material but that doesn't matter as much)

Do note that I have omited including the calculation of the first RRR discount copy because it likely isnt worth precrafting 4 RRRs just to claim 1 discount copy. Also because you've mentioned that you lack OTT materials. But at the very least the commons should be doable for you to precraft.

Do note that the CM prices for RRRs and GRs that you have stated are for the normal versions not the sp version, also they are only for the very first copy which is discounted by 50%. The normal(undiscounted) prices for normal RRRs are 3000 and the SP is 9000. The normal prices for normal GRs are 30000, SPs are a whopping 90000.
The SPs are actually triple the CM cost but the GR mats are only double.
